purpose: DatePicker, DateRangePicker and DateTimePicker: a text field people can type dates (and, for DateTimePicker, times) into, plus a calendar, all honouring the locale's order, separators and clock.
$operationsNote: Mirrors shared/core/agent/field.ts, which is what the runtime dispatches on. source/components/shared/core/agent/__tests__/field-passport.test.ts fails if the two drift. No `apiMethod`: a field is written through its ref — the element for most of these, a handle for Combobox and DatePicker — and that is a normal case, not a gap. Inside an <AgentSurface> the component registers itself with these operations; NumberInput and RadioGroup are then written through their own commit path rather than the element.

setValue.summary: Write a value into the field, as though a person had entered it.

focus.summary: Move keyboard focus to the field.

open.summary: Open the field's calendar or option list.

close.summary: Close the field's calendar or option list.

supplied: the calendar is a grid with arrow keys between days, PageUp/PageDown between months, Home and End within a week
the selected and focused days are distinguished for assistive technology, not only by colour
the field accepts typing, so the calendar is never the only way in
Escape closes the calendar and returns focus to the field
DateTimePicker's hour, minute and second are spin buttons: arrow keys step them, PageUp and PageDown move further, and a screen reader announces each by name and value
on a 12-hour clock the AM/PM switch is a labelled button, toggled by click or by the arrow keys
required: a `label`, or `aria-label` when the field is visually unlabelled
a `locale` matching the user's, since 03/04 is two different days in two places
an `hourCycle` only when the clock should differ from the locale's own; by default 2:30 PM and 14:30 follow `locale`

composition.notes: The calendar renders in the top layer. `presets` are shortcuts into the same value, not a separate control.

safeMutations.rationale: Calendar chrome is presentation. `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` are the rules about which dates are legal, and `format` and `locale` decide how a typed string is read — changing either can reinterpret a date the user already entered. For DateTimePicker, `hourCycle` decides how a typed time is read (2:30 against 14:30), and `defaultTime` is the time a picked day receives — both change values, not looks.

propNotes.format: How a typed string is parsed as well as displayed. Changing it can turn a valid entry into a different day.
propNotes.presets: Labelled shortcuts such as last quarter. They write the same value the calendar does.
propNotes.hourCycle: 12 or 24. Changes how a typed time is read as well as shown; defaults to the locale's clock.
propNotes.minuteStep: How far the minute moves per arrow press. Typed minutes are not snapped to it.
propNotes.min: For DateTimePicker a moment, not a day: earlier days cannot be picked, and on the day itself an earlier time is moved up to it.
